columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Primarily serves associations, professional organizations, and B2B via Higher Logic Thrive (community + marketing automation) and Higher Logic Vanilla (embedded forums).
Thrive Community: member areas, discussions, events, resource libraries, and engagement tools for associations.
Capabilities include forums/Q&A/events, member directory, analytics, personalized communications, AI recommendations, and email/lifecycle automation.

strengths.title: Built for associations and membership organizations
strengths.detail: Tailored to member experience, retention, CE, and advocacy, not generic social groups.

strengths.title: Integrated community + marketing automation
strengths.detail: Member behavior can trigger targeted communications across the stack.

strengths.title: Enterprise-grade features and services
strengths.detail: Implementation support, best-practice guidance, and analytics for large, complex member bases.

weaknesses.title: Enterprise complexity and cost
weaknesses.detail: Implementation, configuration, and pricing can be heavy for small community projects.

weaknesses.title: Less creator-centric than newer platforms
weaknesses.detail: Optimized for associations and B2B, may feel overbuilt for indie creators.

weaknesses.title: Older UI and competition
weaknesses.detail: Competes with newer platforms (Mighty Networks, Bettermode, Disciple, Hivebrite) emphasizing modern UX and flexible monetization.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Higher Logic is enterprise community platforms (including Vanilla) for associations, brands, and large organizations. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Higher Logic is a cloud-based community engagement platform that connects communities, communications, data, and AI into one ecosystem to build, manage, and grow online member and customer communities. Official site.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Higher Logic side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Higher Logic you can use Community & Messaging as a first-class product job. The job is hanging out, announcements, and live conversation, not packaging knowledge into something strangers can browse later.

Using Kahana with Higher Logic

You can use both. Higher Logic keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep live conversation on Higher Logic. Pin a Kahana hub or Club link in a channel, discuss live there, and assign the next ebook, video, or course from Kahana so the syllabus is not buried in the thread.
